title: New trailer and playable free demo available for my Neon Breaker Endless Arcade SHMUP
author: Traditional-Bath1988
selftext:
Updated my Neon Breaker retro 3d shmup solo game project and prepared a new demo plus trailer on Steam in preparation for the upcoming Next Fest  
[https://store.steampowered.com/app/5054650/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5054650/)

Hope everyone likes the tweaked gameplay and polished looked

The game for me is a tribute to the classics i loved growing up, so it must strive to be good

AI played a positive role in allowing me a solo dev to finish/polish multiple aspects without having to get funders for a much bigger budget and hire a team (that beats the point of being a solo dev)

Indeed some online currently opposing AI use fully are conflating things together. 

They are misjudging solo devs or small teams with no budget with AAA studios with hundreds of  million dollars in funding and thousands on their team for using AI

This is not reasonable nor tenable perspective, and i am certain this sentiment will change with time

As for Neon Breaker, the first prototype i made for this game is more than 10 years old and i never got around to wrap the project until now thanks to the affordable opportunities we currently have

Game feel/polish remains the top priority for any video game/app regardless of the tools used

There is no excuse for low effort projects regardless of tools and pipelines

Full game launch scheduled on Steam for end of this month of October

Other platforms soon hopefully as well

Wishlist if you enjoy the trailer and demo!

Peace

comments.author: toiletman74
comments.body: Looks awesome! I did notice that it's hard to keep track of where the player's ship is though

replies.author: Traditional-Bath1988
replies.body: Glad you like it and thank you for the constructive feedback. Yes the clarify of the ship (without making it big like other games did) was one of the challenging aspects tbh, i already added a few helpers (animated dashed focus circle that can be toggled in settings, blinking airplane backlights, and comic style feedback bubbles from the pilots). I am always open to more suggestions, but don't judge just from the video trailer, download the free demo and try it yourself directly as i personally found it somewhat easier to locate the ship when playing. Let me know.
